evil_mirror_analysis.note: This Torah is very brief and focused entirely on the positive path. The evil counterparts are mentioned only in eitza relationships, not as bechina pairs. The structural evil mirror would be: מרה שחורה (depression) as the anti-שמחה, and גלות (exile) as the anti-עולם החרות. However, the text does NOT explicitly equate these evil concepts via bechina language — it describes them only as causal obstacles ('through depression one cannot lead the mind', 'through exile the mind is not settled'). Therefore no evil package can be formally proposed from the bechina evidence alone, but the evil structural mirror is: מרה שחורה ↔ גלות (both are the domain of blocked mochin and spiritual constriction).

analysis_notes.torah_structure_note: LM2 Torah 10 is one of the shortest in the corpus. Its argument is entirely linear (eitza chain): lack of yishuv ha-daat → need for simcha → simcha is cherut → simcha enables the mind to be free → yishuv ha-daat achieved → return to God. The only structural bechina (parallel nature) is at the pivot point: simcha IS freedom (not 'causes' freedom — they are the same thing).
